- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak or adjust downward by 1–2 price points.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model continues to rise, reduce forecast slope; expect mean reversion within 3–5 days.
- When true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >5% below), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if so, apply downward bias correction for next 3–5 days.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than 3-day moving average of history, reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion tendency.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits recent volatility — use 10–15 day smoothing or adjust for lagged sentiment decay.
